Prepared from the Budget Monitor source code, documented Replit Enterprise API behavior, and the data exports embedded in the project. Code citations are file:line in the app source.Comcast Budget Monitor — Discrepancy Report & Remediation Plan
Date: 2026-08-24  ·  Scope: why the Budget Monitor app disagrees with the Replit usage dashboard, on every page — and the tasks that fix it.
Evidence: app source code · documented Replit Enterprise API behavior · the app's own data exports (replit-spend-gap.xlsx, replit-raw-api-spend.xlsx, CSV exports).
Copy full report
0. Headline reconciliation
1. Enterprise API behavior the app must respect
2. Issues with evidence
3. Scoped remediation tasks
4. Comparison guardrails
0.Headline reconciliation — Aug 18 exports
METHOD	TOTAL	SOURCE
Replit Settings → Usage (in-product)	$99,432.19	replit-spend-gap.xlsx · Summary
App dashboard total	$90,707.85	replit-spend-gap.xlsx · Summary
Sum of raw per-group API spend (173 groups)	$105,577.73	replit-raw-api-spend.xlsx · Summary
App MAX-per-user-per-workspace method	$80,760.34	replit-raw-api-spend.xlsx · Summary

Four totals, four accounting models. None is bad arithmetic — they count different things. The $8,724.34 app-vs-Settings gap decomposes into:

spend by the 563 directory users in no custom group (the app never credits them anywhere);
unattributed usage rows — charges carrying no user id (e.g. some deployment/storage and org-level charges);
ex-member spend — e.g. one removed user carried $1,268.89 across two workspaces ("Former Members" sheet).
1.Enterprise API behavior the app must respect

These are properties of the /v1/usage endpoint itself. They are not bugs; the app has to be designed around them.

A1 — An unfiltered call is the source of truth. GET /v1/usage with no workspaceId/groupId returns the account-wide gross usage total — the same figure the Settings → Usage page shows. Group- and workspace-filtered calls return subsets that do not add back up to it (see A2).
A2 — Group filters mean "current members' spend". Filtering by workspaceId + groupId resolves the group's membership at request time and returns those users' spend. Therefore: a member's entire window spend counts (not just spend made while a member); users removed from the group or deleted contribute $0 retroactively; charges with no user attribution are excluded entirely; and users in N groups are counted N times across groups — group totals are not additive.
A3 — Per-member data covers all metric types. groupBy=member includes AI, deployments, storage, etc. — anything attributed to the user. (The in-product per-user table shows Agent spend only, so it will read lower than API per-user totals; the API response includes per-metric detail, so an Agent-only view can be derived if needed.)
A4 — Windows and freshness. startTime is inclusive, endTime exclusive, timestamps honored as given. billingPeriod=current resolves to the account's real billing period. Recent usage can arrive late — different resource types post on different cadences (minutes for AI, up to a few hours for deployments and databases) — so same-minute comparisons will not match to the cent.
A5 — Totals are gross. Usage totals exclude account credits, discounts, and invoice adjustments. Compare against usage views, not billed/owed amounts.
2.Issues, evidence, remediation
Issue 1 — Ungrouped users are invisible: the main dashboard gap high→ T1, T2

The dashboard/summary total only credits spend to users who belong to some custom group. The 563 workspace members in no custom group are dropped entirely.

EVIDENCE

Rollup phase 2 candidate set = directory group members ∪ group API members only (enterprise.ts:1695-1697). getExtraWorkspaceSpend skips every workspace that owns custom groups (enterprise.ts:1379-1384), so ungrouped users inside Comcast/Growth/FTA/Finance-Community are never credited — even though queueAllWorkspacesFetch (enterprise.ts:1363-1372) already downloads their per-user spend. The replit-spend-gap.xlsx analysis reaches the same conclusion ($8,724.34, 563 users).

Issue 2 — Unattributed (no-user) spend dropped almost everywhere high→ T1, T3

Charges with no user id (some deployment/storage and org-level charges) appear in the account-wide total but nowhere in the app.

EVIDENCE

Group-filtered API calls exclude them by construction (behavior A2). The app's workspace-member aggregation reads only byUser and discards the response's totalCostUsd/unattributableTotalCostUsd (enterprise.ts:604-606). The per-group unattributableTotalCostUsd added at enterprise.ts:1689-1691 is ~0 for group-scoped calls because the group filter already removed those rows.

Issue 3 — Ex-member / deleted-user spend silently vanishes medium→ T1

Spend made while a group member disappears from group totals the moment they're removed, so app history drifts downward vs the account-wide total.

EVIDENCE

Behavior A2. "Former Members" sheet: user 60777461 = $1,132.22 + $136.67. Per-group recovery of past spend isn't possible through the API; the account anchor (T1) makes the residual visible as a labeled line item, and a membership-snapshot approach (T11, optional) prevents future losses.

Issue 4 — Four competing accounting models across pages high→ T4, T5, T8

The same "spend" is computed four ways, so pages disagree with each other and each disagrees with the usage dashboard differently. This is the root of the earlier "Dashboard vs Team page" debugging effort.

EVIDENCE
Model 1 (raw group total): trends chart buckets (monitor.ts:1938); team trend series sum them with no dedup (monitor.ts:1954-1959) → double-counts shared users; group alert checker (checker.ts:231-247); group-detail projects footer (monitor.ts:788-790).
Model 2 (deduped first-group rollup): dashboard rows / team headers / group-detail header (monitor.ts:302, 405, 440-452, 709).
Model 3 (project attribution): summary Remaining / over-threshold (monitor.ts:1040-1099) while the client fallback uses model 2 (dashboard.tsx:225-256) — same card, two answers.
Model 4 (MAX within workspace, summed across): trends User Activity (monitor.ts:2221-2254), which also ignores the page range picker (monitor.ts:2131+).
Cluster pages add creator-based project attribution (monitor.ts:885-911) and first-response-wins member merge (cluster-detail.tsx:127-150).
Issue 5 — Equal-amount dedup heuristic medium→ T5

Phase-1 dedup treats two identical per-user dollar amounts from different group fetches as the same observation. Correct within one workspace; wrong across workspaces (coincidentally equal spend is dropped) and wrong when the same workspace's value drifts between serialized fetches (double count).

EVIDENCE

enterprise.ts:1666-1675 — Set<number> of observed amounts per user, no workspace key.

Issue 6 — Per-user numbers don't match the in-product per-user table, or each other medium→ T4, T6

App member rows are all-metric attributed spend; the in-product per-user table shows Agent spend only (behavior A3), so app rows read higher for anyone with non-agent spend. Internally, the app also has three per-user definitions that disagree with each other.

EVIDENCE

Group-detail member rows: raw per-group sums (monitor.ts:642, comment 634-640). rawMemberSpendUsd: MAX path (monitor.ts:360-373). User Activity: model 4. Project scoping example: LocalSERPAnalyzer 1b17c77f = $4,627.27 in the in-product export (spend-per-project.csv) vs $2,046.94 in the app's group-scoped CSV (project-spend-2026-08-21.csv) — group filtering slices project spend to that group's current members.

Issue 7 — "Billing period" is a hardcoded window, not the billing period medium→ T7

The app's default range is 2026-05-20T00:00:00Z → now, never billingPeriod=current. If the account's real billing cycle differs from the May 20 anchor (or someone compares a monthly view in-product), every number shifts.

EVIDENCE

enterprise.ts:78, 141-146; Pace column separately hardcodes 2026-05-20 → 2027-05-17 (dashboard.tsx:8-25); behavior A4.

Issue 8 — Staleness: 48h reconciliation ceiling, frozen custom ranges medium→ T9

Open ranges only re-fetch the trailing 48h; usage restated later never lands. Custom ranges whose end has passed are frozen forever, even though some resource types post hours late — a range ending "today" snapshots too early and never corrects.

EVIDENCE

enterprise.ts:280, 390-393 (overlap); enterprise.ts:367 + isDurablyFresh at :644 (frozen closed ranges); behavior A4 (late-arriving usage).

Issue 9 — Misleading copy; alerts frozen on a different model low→ T4, T10

The "By Group" tab claims raw API spend identical to the detail page but renders rollup spend. Alerts show values frozen at send time, and the checker fires on model 1 while the dashboard shows model 2 — a group can alert at 100% while its dashboard row shows <100%.

EVIDENCE

dashboard.tsx:880; checker.ts:183-199 (frozen values), checker.ts:231-247 (model 1 comparison).

3.Scoped remediation tasks

Each task is a self-contained brief — hand them off one at a time, in order. T1–T3 + T5 close the dashboard gap; T4 removes internal inconsistency; the rest are correctness/clarity hardening. All tasks use only the Enterprise API. Click to expand.

T1
Add an account-wide anchor total from unfiltered /usage
Copy task

Goal: Dashboard "Total Spend" equals the account-wide usage total (behavior A1), with the unattributable remainder shown, not lost.

Change: In enterprise.ts, add a new sync mode account_total that calls /usage with NO workspaceId/groupId (reuse synchronizeUsage with scopeKey="account"). Store totalCostUsd, attributableTotalCostUsd, unattributableTotalCostUsd. In monitor.ts /api/summary, report totalSpendUsd from this account total. Add a derived otherSpendUsd = accountTotal − Σ(rollup attribution) as its own field, rendered on the dashboard as a "Not in any group / unattributed / former members" row (extend the unattributed-projects row pattern at dashboard.tsx:765-790).

Non-goal: do not change per-group rows in this task.

Accept when: /api/summary.totalSpendUsd matches GET /v1/usage (same window, no filters) totalCostUsd within ingestion lag, and the dashboard footer total equals the summary card.
T2
Credit ungrouped users inside grouped workspaces
Copy task

Goal: The 563 directory users with no custom group stop being dropped from rollup-based totals.

Change: In getDedupedUsageRollup (enterprise.ts:1638-1721), after phase 2, iterate wsSpendCache per workspace (data already fetched by queueAllWorkspacesFetch) and collect users not in seenUsers. Attribute them to a synthetic pseudo-group per workspace (e.g. __ungrouped__:<wsId>) included in byGroup and totalSpendUsd. Surface as one "No group" row per workspace (or a single account row); do NOT fold into a real group's number. Rewire extra-workspace dedup to use per-workspace values rather than a pre-summed map (feeds T5).

Accept when: Sum of all dashboard rows (groups + No-group rows + unattributed) = T1 account anchor minus unattributable-only residual; re-running the gap-users methodology from replit-spend-gap.xlsx returns ~0 users.
T3
Stop discarding workspace-level unattributed spend
Copy task

Goal: Capture org-level charges with no user id, per workspace.

Change: aggregateWorkspaceMemberUsage (enterprise.ts:604-606) currently returns only byUser. Make the workspace_member cache store the full MemberUsage (the type already exists) including totalCostUsd and unattributableTotalCostUsd; expose workspaceUnattributedUsd = totalCostUsd − Σ byUser per workspace. Include it in the T2 "No group" row (or a dedicated "Workspace unattributed" line) and in the summary reconciliation.

Accept when: For each workspace, app-reported byUser sum + unattributed = that workspace's unfiltered /usage?workspaceId=X totalCostUsd (spot-check 3 workspaces).
T4
One attribution model everywhere
Copy task

Goal: Every surface showing "group spend", "team spend", or "remaining" uses the same rollup (post T2/T3/T5), eliminating cross-page disagreement.

Change: Introduce one shared getCanonicalRollup(rangeKey) in enterprise.ts returning deduped rollup + project attribution + account anchor. Convert:

/api/summary Remaining/over-threshold (monitor.ts:1040-1099) from project-attributed spend to rollup spend; delete the divergent client fallback math in dashboard.tsx:217-256 in favor of server fields.
Trends team series (monitor.ts:1954-1959): compute per-bucket team values from deduped member data, not summed raw group totals.
Checker group alerts (checker.ts:231-247): compare budgets against rollup group spend (the number the dashboard row shows); keep the existing team-alert rollup path.
Cluster Total/Member cards: derive from the same rollup byGroup/byUser maps instead of first-response-wins merging (cluster-detail.tsx:127-150).

Non-goal: project-level attribution semantics unchanged (project tables keep model 3; only headline/rollup surfaces unify).

Accept when: For 5 teams, Dashboard team header = Team page member-spend total = trends final cumulative point (same range), and no alert fires at a % that disagrees with the dashboard row's %.
T5
Exact dedup keyed by (userId, workspaceId)
Copy task

Goal: Replace the equal-amount heuristic with exact dedup.

Change: In phase 1 of getDedupedUsageRollup (enterprise.ts:1651-1676), key observations by (userId, group.workspaceId) and keep ONE value per key (latest fetch wins), then sum across workspaces per user. Remove the Set<number> amount matching. Each MemberUsage needs its group's workspaceId — already available from the EnterpriseGroup in ordered. (This is exact because under a group filter, a user's per-member value IS their workspace total — behavior A2.)

Accept when: Unit tests pass for: (a) user in 2 groups same workspace → counted once; (b) user in 2 workspaces with equal spend → counted twice; (c) same-workspace values drifting between fetches → latest value used once. Current code fails (b) (drops) and (c) (double-counts).
T6
Correct per-user semantics and labels
Copy task

Goal: Per-user numbers internally consistent and honestly labeled vs the in-product Agent-only table.

Change:

Delete the false-premise comment and the MAX(group_member, workspace_member) path (monitor.ts:356-373) — under a group filter a user's value already equals their workspace total (behavior A2), so the MAX is a no-op within one workspace. Replace rawMemberSpendUsd with rollup per-user values.
Make trends User Activity (monitor.ts:2131+) respect the page's selected range and read the same rollup byUser map (removes model 4).
Add a UI caption to member tables: "All metric types (AI, deployments, storage). Replit's in-product per-user table shows Agent spend only and will read lower."
Accept when: Group-detail member row = User Activity row = cluster member row for the same user and range.
T7
Verify the billing window against the real billing period
Copy task

Goal: Confirm or fix the hardcoded May 20 anchor.

Change: On server start (and daily), call /v1/usage?billingPeriod=current&groupBy=timeseries&limit=1 (cheap) and store interval.startTime/endTime. Expose in /api/status and on the Settings page. If the billing period start ≠ 2026-05-20, show a visible warning banner; keep cutoff behavior otherwise. Replace the hardcoded Pace window (dashboard.tsx:8-25) with the fetched period bounds when available.

Accept when: Settings shows the true billing period, and it matches (or a warning explains) the app's default window.
T8
Trends bucket reconciliation disclosure
Copy task

Goal: Trend series sums reconcile with dashboard totals for the same window.

Change: After T4.2, add a reconciliation note/tooltip where bucket sums can still differ from the headline (ingestion lag on the current bucket; UTC day quantization). Mark the current (open) bucket visibly partial.

Accept when: Σ weekly buckets for a closed period equals the dashboard total for the same custom range, for 3 sampled teams.
T9
Reconciliation window and frozen snapshots
Copy task

Goal: Late-posted usage and restatements eventually land.

Change: In enterprise.ts: (a) raise RECONCILIATION_OVERLAP_MS from 48 h to 7 d for open ranges (still daily chunks); (b) for closed custom ranges, do not mark isClosed until end + 24h (rangeBounds, enterprise.ts:359-369); (c) add an admin-only "force full resync" per range that clears that rangeKey's sync state rows.

Accept when: A custom range ending yesterday refreshes at least once more today; forced resync visibly re-pulls a full range.
T10
Honest copy and alert context
Copy task

Goal: Kill misleading labels.

Change: Fix the "By Group" header copy (dashboard.tsx:880) to say "member-deduped attributed spend (same as group detail header)". On the Alerts page, label stored values "snapshot at send time" and show current spend alongside (live rollup value for the group id).

Accept when: No page claims two numbers are the same source unless they call the same function.
T11
(Optional) Daily membership snapshots for stable group history
Copy task

Goal: Group and team history stops rewriting itself when members are removed (behavior A2 means the API can't do this for you).

Change: The app already syncs usage in daily chunks and caches the directory. Snapshot each group's member list once per day into a DB table. When building historical group/team series, attribute each day's per-user spend against that day's roster instead of the current roster. Current-period live numbers keep using live membership.

Accept when: Removing a test user from a group changes no historical daily values for that group; only days after removal drop them.
4.Comparison guardrails (process, not code)
Reconcile app numbers against Settings → Usage (or an unfiltered /v1/usage call). Billing/invoice views show net amounts after credits and discounts, which the usage API intentionally excludes (behavior A5) — they will always differ.
Never compare same-minute: usage posts on different cadences per resource type (behavior A4) — allow a few hours for deployment/database spend to settle.
When comparing per-user numbers in-product, remember the in-product table is Agent-only (behavior A3); the API and this app count all metric types.

Goal: Every surface showing "group spend", "team spend", or "remaining" uses the same rollup (post T2/T3/T5), eliminating cross-page disagreement.

Change: Introduce one shared getCanonicalRollup(rangeKey) in enterprise.ts returning deduped rollup + project attribution + account anchor. Convert:

/api/summary Remaining/over-threshold (monitor.ts:1040-1099) from project-attributed spend to rollup spend; delete the divergent client fallback math in dashboard.tsx:217-256 in favor of server fields.
Trends team series (monitor.ts:1954-1959): compute per-bucket team values from deduped member data, not summed raw group totals.
Checker group alerts (checker.ts:231-247): compare budgets against rollup group spend (the number the dashboard row shows); keep the existing team-alert rollup path.
Cluster Total/Member cards: derive from the same rollup byGroup/byUser maps instead of first-response-wins merging (cluster-detail.tsx:127-150).

Non-goal: project-level attribution semantics unchanged (project tables keep model 3; only headline/rollup surfaces unify).

Accept when: For 5 teams, Dashboard team header = Team page member-spend total = trends final cumulative point (same range), and no alert fires at a % that disagrees with the dashboard row's %.
T5
Exact dedup keyed by (userId, workspaceId)
Copy task

Goal: Replace the equal-amount heuristic with exact dedup.

Change: In phase 1 of getDedupedUsageRollup (enterprise.ts:1651-1676), key observations by (userId, group.workspaceId) and keep ONE value per key (latest fetch wins), then sum across workspaces per user. Remove the Set<number> amount matching. Each MemberUsage needs its group's workspaceId — already available from the EnterpriseGroup in ordered. (This is exact because under a group filter, a user's per-member value IS their workspace total — behavior A2.)

Accept when: Unit tests pass for: (a) user in 2 groups same workspace → counted once; (b) user in 2 workspaces with equal spend → counted twice; (c) same-workspace values drifting between fetches → latest value used once. Current code fails (b) (drops) and (c) (double-counts).
T6
Correct per-user semantics and labels
Copy task

Goal: Per-user numbers internally consistent and honestly labeled vs the in-product Agent-only table.

Change:

Delete the false-premise comment and the MAX(group_member, workspace_member) path (monitor.ts:356-373) — under a group filter a user's value already equals their workspace total (behavior A2), so the MAX is a no-op within one workspace. Replace rawMemberSpendUsd with rollup per-user values.
Make trends User Activity (monitor.ts:2131+) respect the page's selected range and read the same rollup byUser map (removes model 4).
Add a UI caption to member tables: "All metric types (AI, deployments, storage). Replit's in-product per-user table shows Agent spend only and will read lower."
Accept when: Group-detail member row = User Activity row = cluster member row for the same user and range.
T7
Verify the billing window against the real billing period
Copy task

Goal: Confirm or fix the hardcoded May 20 anchor.

Change: On server start (and daily), call /v1/usage?billingPeriod=current&groupBy=timeseries&limit=1 (cheap) and store interval.startTime/endTime. Expose in /api/status and on the Settings page. If the billing period start ≠ 2026-05-20, show a visible warning banner; keep cutoff behavior otherwise. Replace the hardcoded Pace window (dashboard.tsx:8-25) with the fetched period bounds when available.

Accept when: Settings shows the true billing period, and it matches (or a warning explains) the app's default window.
T8
Trends bucket reconciliation disclosure
Copy task

Goal: Trend series sums reconcile with dashboard totals for the same window.

Change: After T4.2, add a reconciliation note/tooltip where bucket sums can still differ from the headline (ingestion lag on the current bucket; UTC day quantization). Mark the current (open) bucket visibly partial.

Accept when: Σ weekly buckets for a closed period equals the dashboard total for the same custom range, for 3 sampled teams.
T9
Reconciliation window and frozen snapshots
Copy task

Goal: Late-posted usage and restatements eventually land.

Change: In enterprise.ts: (a) raise RECONCILIATION_OVERLAP_MS from 48 h to 7 d for open ranges (still daily chunks); (b) for closed custom ranges, do not mark isClosed until end + 24h (rangeBounds, enterprise.ts:359-369); (c) add an admin-only "force full resync" per range that clears that rangeKey's sync state rows.

Accept when: A custom range ending yesterday refreshes at least once more today; forced resync visibly re-pulls a full range.
T10
Honest copy and alert context
Copy task

Goal: Kill misleading labels.

Change: Fix the "By Group" header copy (dashboard.tsx:880) to say "member-deduped attributed spend (same as group detail header)". On the Alerts page, label stored values "snapshot at send time" and show current spend alongside (live rollup value for the group id).

Accept when: No page claims two numbers are the same source unless they call the same function.
T11
(Optional) Daily membership snapshots for stable group history
Copy task

Goal: Group and team history stops rewriting itself when members are removed (behavior A2 means the API can't do this for you).

Change: The app already syncs usage in daily chunks and caches the directory. Snapshot each group's member list once per day into a DB table. When building historical group/team series, attribute each day's per-user spend against that day's roster instead of the current roster. Current-period live numbers keep using live membership.

Accept when: Removing a test user from a group changes no historical daily values for that group; only days after removal drop them.
4.Comparison guardrails (process, not code)
Reconcile app numbers against Settings → Usage (or an unfiltered /v1/usage call). Billing/invoice views show net amounts after credits and discounts, which the usage API intentionally excludes (behavior A5) — they will always differ.
Never compare same-minute: usage posts on different cadences per resource type (behavior A4) — allow a few hours for deployment/database spend to settle.
When comparing per-user numbers in-product, remember the in-product table is Agent-only (behavior A3); the API and this app count all metric types.

Prepared from the Budget Monitor source code, documented Replit Enterprise API behavior, and the data exports embedded in the project. Code citations are file:line in the app source.Comcast Budget Monitor — Discrepancy Report & Remediation Plan
Date: 2026-08-24  ·  Scope: why the Budget Monitor app disagrees with the Replit usage dashboard, on every page — and the tasks that fix it.
Evidence: app source code · documented Replit Enterprise API behavior · the app's own data exports (replit-spend-gap.xlsx, replit-raw-api-spend.xlsx, CSV exports).
Copy full report
0. Headline reconciliation
1. Enterprise API behavior the app must respect
2. Issues with evidence
3. Scoped remediation tasks
4. Comparison guardrails
0.Headline reconciliation — Aug 18 exports
METHOD	TOTAL	SOURCE
Replit Settings → Usage (in-product)	$99,432.19	replit-spend-gap.xlsx · Summary
App dashboard total	$90,707.85	replit-spend-gap.xlsx · Summary
Sum of raw per-group API spend (173 groups)	$105,577.73	replit-raw-api-spend.xlsx · Summary
App MAX-per-user-per-workspace method	$80,760.34	replit-raw-api-spend.xlsx · Summary

Four totals, four accounting models. None is bad arithmetic — they count different things. The $8,724.34 app-vs-Settings gap decomposes into:

spend by the 563 directory users in no custom group (the app never credits them anywhere);
unattributed usage rows — charges carrying no user id (e.g. some deployment/storage and org-level charges);
ex-member spend — e.g. one removed user carried $1,268.89 across two workspaces ("Former Members" sheet).
1.Enterprise API behavior the app must respect

These are properties of the /v1/usage endpoint itself. They are not bugs; the app has to be designed around them.

A1 — An unfiltered call is the source of truth. GET /v1/usage with no workspaceId/groupId returns the account-wide gross usage total — the same figure the Settings → Usage page shows. Group- and workspace-filtered calls return subsets that do not add back up to it (see A2).
A2 — Group filters mean "current members' spend". Filtering by workspaceId + groupId resolves the group's membership at request time and returns those users' spend. Therefore: a member's entire window spend counts (not just spend made while a member); users removed from the group or deleted contribute $0 retroactively; charges with no user attribution are excluded entirely; and users in N groups are counted N times across groups — group totals are not additive.
A3 — Per-member data covers all metric types. groupBy=member includes AI, deployments, storage, etc. — anything attributed to the user. (The in-product per-user table shows Agent spend only, so it will read lower than API per-user totals; the API response includes per-metric detail, so an Agent-only view can be derived if needed.)
A4 — Windows and freshness. startTime is inclusive, endTime exclusive, timestamps honored as given. billingPeriod=current resolves to the account's real billing period. Recent usage can arrive late — different resource types post on different cadences (minutes for AI, up to a few hours for deployments and databases) — so same-minute comparisons will not match to the cent.
A5 — Totals are gross. Usage totals exclude account credits, discounts, and invoice adjustments. Compare against usage views, not billed/owed amounts.
2.Issues, evidence, remediation
Issue 1 — Ungrouped users are invisible: the main dashboard gap high→ T1, T2

The dashboard/summary total only credits spend to users who belong to some custom group. The 563 workspace members in no custom group are dropped entirely.

EVIDENCE

Rollup phase 2 candidate set = directory group members ∪ group API members only (enterprise.ts:1695-1697). getExtraWorkspaceSpend skips every workspace that owns custom groups (enterprise.ts:1379-1384), so ungrouped users inside Comcast/Growth/FTA/Finance-Community are never credited — even though queueAllWorkspacesFetch (enterprise.ts:1363-1372) already downloads their per-user spend. The replit-spend-gap.xlsx analysis reaches the same conclusion ($8,724.34, 563 users).

Issue 2 — Unattributed (no-user) spend dropped almost everywhere high→ T1, T3

Charges with no user id (some deployment/storage and org-level charges) appear in the account-wide total but nowhere in the app.

EVIDENCE

Group-filtered API calls exclude them by construction (behavior A2). The app's workspace-member aggregation reads only byUser and discards the response's totalCostUsd/unattributableTotalCostUsd (enterprise.ts:604-606). The per-group unattributableTotalCostUsd added at enterprise.ts:1689-1691 is ~0 for group-scoped calls because the group filter already removed those rows.

Issue 3 — Ex-member / deleted-user spend silently vanishes medium→ T1

Spend made while a group member disappears from group totals the moment they're removed, so app history drifts downward vs the account-wide total.

EVIDENCE

Behavior A2. "Former Members" sheet: user 60777461 = $1,132.22 + $136.67. Per-group recovery of past spend isn't possible through the API; the account anchor (T1) makes the residual visible as a labeled line item, and a membership-snapshot approach (T11, optional) prevents future losses.

Issue 4 — Four competing accounting models across pages high→ T4, T5, T8

The same "spend" is computed four ways, so pages disagree with each other and each disagrees with the usage dashboard differently. This is the root of the earlier "Dashboard vs Team page" debugging effort.

EVIDENCE
Model 1 (raw group total): trends chart buckets (monitor.ts:1938); team trend series sum them with no dedup (monitor.ts:1954-1959) → double-counts shared users; group alert checker (checker.ts:231-247); group-detail projects footer (monitor.ts:788-790).
Model 2 (deduped first-group rollup): dashboard rows / team headers / group-detail header (monitor.ts:302, 405, 440-452, 709).
Model 3 (project attribution): summary Remaining / over-threshold (monitor.ts:1040-1099) while the client fallback uses model 2 (dashboard.tsx:225-256) — same card, two answers.
Model 4 (MAX within workspace, summed across): trends User Activity (monitor.ts:2221-2254), which also ignores the page range picker (monitor.ts:2131+).
Cluster pages add creator-based project attribution (monitor.ts:885-911) and first-response-wins member merge (cluster-detail.tsx:127-150).
Issue 5 — Equal-amount dedup heuristic medium→ T5

Phase-1 dedup treats two identical per-user dollar amounts from different group fetches as the same observation. Correct within one workspace; wrong across workspaces (coincidentally equal spend is dropped) and wrong when the same workspace's value drifts between serialized fetches (double count).

EVIDENCE

enterprise.ts:1666-1675 — Set<number> of observed amounts per user, no workspace key.

Issue 6 — Per-user numbers don't match the in-product per-user table, or each other medium→ T4, T6

App member rows are all-metric attributed spend; the in-product per-user table shows Agent spend only (behavior A3), so app rows read higher for anyone with non-agent spend. Internally, the app also has three per-user definitions that disagree with each other.

EVIDENCE

Group-detail member rows: raw per-group sums (monitor.ts:642, comment 634-640). rawMemberSpendUsd: MAX path (monitor.ts:360-373). User Activity: model 4. Project scoping example: LocalSERPAnalyzer 1b17c77f = $4,627.27 in the in-product export (spend-per-project.csv) vs $2,046.94 in the app's group-scoped CSV (project-spend-2026-08-21.csv) — group filtering slices project spend to that group's current members.

Issue 7 — "Billing period" is a hardcoded window, not the billing period medium→ T7

The app's default range is 2026-05-20T00:00:00Z → now, never billingPeriod=current. If the account's real billing cycle differs from the May 20 anchor (or someone compares a monthly view in-product), every number shifts.

EVIDENCE

enterprise.ts:78, 141-146; Pace column separately hardcodes 2026-05-20 → 2027-05-17 (dashboard.tsx:8-25); behavior A4.

Issue 8 — Staleness: 48h reconciliation ceiling, frozen custom ranges medium→ T9

Open ranges only re-fetch the trailing 48h; usage restated later never lands. Custom ranges whose end has passed are frozen forever, even though some resource types post hours late — a range ending "today" snapshots too early and never corrects.

EVIDENCE

enterprise.ts:280, 390-393 (overlap); enterprise.ts:367 + isDurablyFresh at :644 (frozen closed ranges); behavior A4 (late-arriving usage).

Issue 9 — Misleading copy; alerts frozen on a different model low→ T4, T10

The "By Group" tab claims raw API spend identical to the detail page but renders rollup spend. Alerts show values frozen at send time, and the checker fires on model 1 while the dashboard shows model 2 — a group can alert at 100% while its dashboard row shows <100%.

EVIDENCE

dashboard.tsx:880; checker.ts:183-199 (frozen values), checker.ts:231-247 (model 1 comparison).

3.Scoped remediation tasks

Each task is a self-contained brief — hand them off one at a time, in order. T1–T3 + T5 close the dashboard gap; T4 removes internal inconsistency; the rest are correctness/clarity hardening. All tasks use only the Enterprise API. Click to expand.

T1
Add an account-wide anchor total from unfiltered /usage
Copy task

Goal: Dashboard "Total Spend" equals the account-wide usage total (behavior A1), with the unattributable remainder shown, not lost.

Change: In enterprise.ts, add a new sync mode account_total that calls /usage with NO workspaceId/groupId (reuse synchronizeUsage with scopeKey="account"). Store totalCostUsd, attributableTotalCostUsd, unattributableTotalCostUsd. In monitor.ts /api/summary, report totalSpendUsd from this account total. Add a derived otherSpendUsd = accountTotal − Σ(rollup attribution) as its own field, rendered on the dashboard as a "Not in any group / unattributed / former members" row (extend the unattributed-projects row pattern at dashboard.tsx:765-790).

Non-goal: do not change per-group rows in this task.

Accept when: /api/summary.totalSpendUsd matches GET /v1/usage (same window, no filters) totalCostUsd within ingestion lag, and the dashboard footer total equals the summary card.
T2
Credit ungrouped users inside grouped workspaces
Copy task

Attribute them to a synthetic pseudo-group per workspace (e.g. __ungrouped__:<wsId>) included in byGroup and totalSpendUsd. Surface as one "No group" row per workspace (or a single account row); do NOT fold into a real group's number. Rewire extra-workspace dedup to use per-workspace values rather than a pre-summed map (feeds T5).

Accept when: Sum of all dashboard rows (groups + No-group rows + unattributed) = T1 account anchor minus unattributable-only residual; re-running the gap-users methodology from replit-spend-gap.xlsx returns ~0 users.
T3

Copy task

Model 4 (MAX within workspace, summed across): trends User Activity (monitor.ts:2221-2254), which also ignores the page range picker (monitor.ts:2131+).
Cluster pages add creator-based project attribution (monitor.ts:885-911) and first-response-wins member merge (cluster-detail.tsx:127-150).
Issue 5 — Equal-amount dedup heuristic medium→ T5

Phase-1 dedup treats two identical per-user dollar amounts from different group fetches as the same observation. Correct within one workspace; wrong across workspaces (coincidentally equal spend is dropped) and wrong when the same workspace's value drifts between serialized fetches (double count).

EVIDENCE

enterprise.ts:1666-1675 — Set<number> of observed amounts per user, no workspace key.

Issue 6 — Per-user numbers don't match the in-product per-user table, or each other medium→ T4, T6

App member rows are all-metric attributed spend; the in-product per-user table shows Agent spend only (behavior A3), so app rows read higher for anyone with non-agent spend. Internally, the app also has three per-user definitions that disagree with each other.

EVIDENCE

Group-detail member rows: raw per-group sums (monitor.ts:642, comment 634-640). rawMemberSpendUsd: MAX path (monitor.ts:360-373). User Activity: model 4. Project scoping example: LocalSERPAnalyzer 1b17c77f = $4,627.27 in the in-product export (spend-per-project.csv) vs $2,046.94 in the app's group-scoped CSV (project-spend-2026-08-21.csv) — group filtering slices project spend to that group's current members.

Issue 7 — "Billing period" is a hardcoded window, not the billing period medium→ T7

The app's default range is 2026-05-20T00:00:00Z → now, never billingPeriod=current. If the account's real billing cycle differs from the May 20 anchor (or someone compares a monthly view in-product), every number shifts.

EVIDENCE

enterprise.ts:78, 141-146; Pace column separately hardcodes 2026-05-20 → 2027-05-17 (dashboard.tsx:8-25); behavior A4.

Issue 8 — Staleness: 48h reconciliation ceiling, frozen custom ranges medium→ T9

Open ranges only re-fetch the trailing 48h; usage restated later never lands. Custom ranges whose end has passed are frozen forever, even though some resource types post hours late — a range ending "today" snapshots too early and never corrects.

EVIDENCE

enterprise.ts:280, 390-393 (overlap); enterprise.ts:367 + isDurablyFresh at :644 (frozen closed ranges); behavior A4 (late-arriving usage).

Issue 9 — Misleading copy; alerts frozen on a different model low→ T4, T10

The "By Group" tab claims raw API spend identical to the detail page but renders rollup spend. Alerts show values frozen at send time, and the checker fires on model 1 while the dashboard shows model 2 — a group can alert at 100% while its dashboard row shows <100%.

EVIDENCE

dashboard.tsx:880; checker.ts:183-199 (frozen values), checker.ts:231-247 (model 1 comparison).

3.Scoped remediation tasks

Each task is a self-contained brief — hand them off one at a time, in order. T1–T3 + T5 close the dashboard gap; T4 removes internal inconsistency; the rest are correctness/clarity hardening. All tasks use only the Enterprise API. Click to expand.

T1
Add an account-wide anchor total from unfiltered /usage
Copy task

Goal: Dashboard "Total Spend" equals the account-wide usage total (behavior A1), with the unattributable remainder shown, not lost.

Change: In enterprise.ts, add a new sync mode account_total that calls /usage with NO workspaceId/groupId (reuse synchronizeUsage with scopeKey="account"). Store totalCostUsd, attributableTotalCostUsd, unattributableTotalCostUsd. In monitor.ts /api/summary, report totalSpendUsd from this account total. Add a derived otherSpendUsd = accountTotal − Σ(rollup attribution) as its own field, rendered on the dashboard as a "Not in any group / unattributed / former members" row (extend the unattributed-projects row pattern at dashboard.tsx:765-790).

Non-goal: do not change per-group rows in this task.

Accept when: /api/summary.totalSpendUsd matches GET /v1/usage (same window, no filters) totalCostUsd within ingestion lag, and the dashboard footer total equals the summary card.
T2
Credit ungrouped users inside grouped workspaces
Copy task

Goal: The 563 directory users with no custom group stop being dropped from rollup-based totals.

Change: In getDedupedUsageRollup (enterprise.ts:1638-1721), after phase 2, iterate wsSpendCache per workspace (data already fetched by queueAllWorkspacesFetch) and collect users not in seenUsers. Attribute them to a synthetic pseudo-group per workspace (e.g. __ungrouped__:<wsId>) included in byGroup and totalSpendUsd. Surface as one "No group" row per workspace (or a single account row); do NOT fold into a real group's number. Rewire extra-workspace dedup to use per-workspace values rather than a pre-summed map (feeds T5).

Accept when: Sum of all dashboard rows (groups + No-group rows + unattributed) = T1 account anchor minus unattributable-only residual; re-running the gap-users methodology from replit-spend-gap.xlsx returns ~0 users.
T3
Stop discarding workspace-level unattributed spend
Copy task

Goal: Capture org-level charges with no user id, per workspace.

Change: aggregateWorkspaceMemberUsage (enterprise.ts:604-606) currently returns only byUser. Make the workspace_member cache store the full MemberUsage (the type already exists) including totalCostUsd and unattributableTotalCostUsd; expose workspaceUnattributedUsd = totalCostUsd − Σ byUser per workspace. Include it in the T2 "No group" row (or a dedicated "Workspace unattributed" line) and in the summary reconciliation.

Accept when: For each workspace, app-reported byUser sum + unattributed = that workspace's unfiltered /usage?workspaceId=X totalCostUsd (spot-check 3 workspaces).
T4
One attribution model everywhere
Copy task

Goal: Every surface showing "group spend", "team spend", or "remaining" uses the same rollup (post T2/T3/T5), eliminating cross-page disagreement.

Change: Introduce one shared getCanonicalRollup(rangeKey) in enterprise.ts returning deduped rollup + project attribution + account anchor. Convert:

/api/summary Remaining/over-threshold (monitor.ts:1040-1099) from project-attributed spend to rollup spend; delete the divergent client fallback math in dashboard.tsx:217-256 in favor of server fields.
Trends team series (monitor.ts:1954-1959): compute per-bucket team values from deduped member data, not summed raw group totals.
Checker group alerts (checker.ts:231-247): compare budgets against rollup group spend (the number the dashboard row shows); keep the existing team-alert rollup path.
Cluster Total/Member cards: derive from the same rollup byGroup/byUser maps instead of first-response-wins merging (cluster-detail.tsx:127-150).

Non-goal: project-level attribution semantics unchanged (project tables keep model 3; only headline/rollup surfaces unify).

Accept when: For 5 teams, Dashboard team header = Team page member-spend total = trends final cumulative point (same range), and no alert fires at a % that disagrees with the dashboard row's %.
T5
Exact dedup keyed by (userId, workspaceId)
Copy task

Goal: Replace the equal-amount heuristic with exact dedup.

Change: In phase 1 of getDedupedUsageRollup (enterprise.ts:1651-1676), key observations by (userId, group.workspaceId) and keep ONE value per key (latest fetch wins), then sum across workspaces per user. Remove the Set<number> amount matching. Each MemberUsage needs its group's workspaceId — already available from the EnterpriseGroup in ordered. (This is exact because under a group filter, a user's per-member value IS their workspace total — behavior A2.)

Accept when: Unit tests pass for: (a) user in 2 groups same workspace → counted once; (b) user in 2 workspaces with equal spend → counted twice; (c) same-workspace values drifting between fetches → latest value used once. Current code fails (b) (drops) and (c) (double-counts).

Goal: Group and team history stops rewriting itself when members are removed (behavior A2 means the API can't do this for you).

4.Comparison guardrails (process, not code)
Reconcile app numbers against Settings → Usage (or an unfiltered /v1/usage call). Billing/invoice views show net amounts after credits and discounts, which the usage API intentionally excludes (behavior A5) — they will always differ.
Never compare same-minute: usage posts on different cadences per resource type (behavior A4) — allow a few hours for deployment/database spend to settle.
When comparing per-user numbers in-product, remember the in-product table is Agent-only (behavior A3); the API and this app count all metric types.

Prepared from the Budget Monitor source code, documented Replit Enterprise API behavior, and the data exports embedded in the project. Code citations are file:line in the app source.
